# Integrate chat agents (non-Zoom) with actions and triggers

<!-- WARNING: THIS FILE WAS AUTOGENERATED! DO NOT EDIT! -->

Zoom Contact Center supports integrating non-Zoom chat agent platforms and homegrown AI agents into chat flows through Zoom Marketplace apps. You can connect a chat agent that a third-party provider builds and hosts, or one that you build and host. If you're working with a third-party chat agent provider, share this documentation with them and review whether they can connect their chat agent to the Zoom virtual agent framework.

By integrating your chat agent with Zoom Contact Center, you gain access to a full suite of engagement capabilities including chat and messaging capabilities, video escalation, cobrowsing, and screen sharing. Your chat agent can leverage Contact Center's intelligent routing and queue management to seamlessly transition conversations to live agents, while providing unified analytics and reporting across all engagement channels.

Zoom provides the consumer user interface through the Zoom Contact Center web SDK and handles orchestration. Any chat agent that can interface with the virtual agent framework can plug in through the bot widget and route through the bot flow.

Using **action and trigger** mode, your app will be visible in the bot widget and you can route chat engagements to external chat agents that provide automated responses and hand off conversations to live agents when needed through the bot flow.

Action and trigger mode provides two integration capabilities:

-   **Action (synchronous)** - Contact Center sends a consumer message to your chat agent and waits for a response
-   **Trigger (asynchronous)** - Your chat agent pushes replies back to Contact Center asynchronously for long-running operations

Actions can standalone for immediate chat agent responses. Triggers must be paired with actions and are used when your chat agent needs additional processing time.

## Prerequisites

Before you begin, ensure you have the following:

-   Admin role with **Zoom for developers** permission enabled. For more information, see [Check role permissions](/docs/build-flow/before-you-build/#check-role-permissions) in the _Build your app_ guide.
-   Chatbot action mode enabled. For more information, contact Zoom technical support.
-   Contact Center Admin role for Flow, Queue, and Entry Point configuration
-   Access to Contact Center Management > Roles

## Create and configure the Marketplace app

Create a General App on Zoom Marketplace and configure it for Contact Center chat agent integration.

### Create the app

Create a new General App on Zoom Marketplace.

1. Sign in to [Zoom Marketplace](https://marketplace.zoom.us/).
2. Choose **Develop** and then **Build app**.
3. Choose **General App** and then **Create**.
4. (Optional) Rename your app.

### Configure app type

Change the app to admin-managed mode, which is required for Contact Center chat agent integration.

1. In the navigation pane, choose **Basic Information**.
2. In the **Select how the app is managed** section, select **Admin-managed**.
3. Choose **Save**.

### Add a custom form (optional)

If your chat agent requires connection-level configuration (such as botId or projectId), add a custom form.

1. In the navigation pane, choose **Custom Form**.
2. Add your configuration fields.
3. In the **Field setting levels**, select **Connection-level**.
4. Choose **Save Changes**.

### Configure base URL and authentication

Set up the base URL and authentication method for your chat agent API.

1. In the navigation pane, choose **Connect**.
2. Choose **Base URL & authentication**.
3. Enter your Base URL (for example, `https://your-bot-platform.com/api`).
4. Select your authentication method (API Key, OAuth 2.0, Basic Auth, Bearer Token, or JWT Bearer).
5. Configure the authentication credentials.
6. Choose **Save changes**.

## Configure the action

Actions define how Contact Center sends messages to your chat agent and transforms the responses.

### Add an endpoint

Create an endpoint that Contact Center will call to send messages to your chat agent.

1. In the navigation pane, choose **Connect**.
2. Choose **Endpoints**.
3. Choose **+ New endpoint**.
4. Configure the endpoint:
    - **Method**: POST
    - **Display name**: `send_message_to_bot`
    - **Endpoint path**: `/send_message_to_bot`
    - **Parameters**: Leave empty
5. Choose **Save**.

The complete endpoint URL will be your Base URL combined with the endpoint path (for example, `https://your-bot-platform.com/api/send_message_to_bot`).

### Create the action

Use the actions wizard to configure how Contact Center interacts with your chat agent.

1. In the navigation pane, choose **Actions and Triggers**.
2. Choose **+ New action**.
3. Select **Built-in actions**.

> **Note**
>
> If you don't see **Built-in actions** as an option, verify that Chatbot action mode has been enabled for your account. Contact Zoom technical support to enable this feature.

4. In the action dropdown, select `zcc.chatbot_send_message_to_bot`.
5. Choose **Next**.
6. On the access page, verify **Contact Center Chatbot** is checked and choose **Next**.
7. On the Form Builder page, use the predefined fields and choose **Next**.
8. On the Transformations page:
    - In UI mode, select your endpoint from the dropdown
    - Switch to **Script** mode
    - Write your transformation script (see examples below)
9. Optionally test your action, then choose **Finish**.

### Write the transformation script

The transformation script converts between Contact Center's message format and your chat agent's API format.

#### Available APIs

Use these APIs in your transformation script.

-   `ctx.inputData` - Access Contact Center input fields
-   `zm.fetch({ url, method, data })` - Make HTTP requests to your endpoint
-   `zm.handleResponse(result, successFn, errorFn)` - Handle responses (2xx/3xx codes trigger success function)
-   `zm.log.info('message {}', value)` - Log messages using `{}` placeholders

#### Input format (Contact Center to chat agent)

Contact Center sends messages to your chat agent in this format.

```json
{
    "id": "msg-001",
    "sessionId": "sess-abc-123",
    "conversationMode": "START_CONVERSATION",
    "message": { "type": "text", "value": "hi" },
    "conversationVariables": {
        "global_system.Engagement.timezone": "America/New_York"
    },
    "additionalPayload": null,
    "languageCode": "en-US",
    "timestamp": 1700000000000,
    "userId": "user-xyz-789",
    "customData": {
        "botId": "bot-001",
        "flowId": "flow-001",
        "signature": "<zcc-injected-signature>",
        "connectionId": "conn-001"
    }
}
```

Key fields:

-   `conversationVariables` - Only populated on `START_CONVERSATION`, empty `{}` on subsequent messages
-   `additionalPayload` - `null` for text messages, contains interaction data for forms/cards/quick replies
-   `message.type` - Can be text, html, markdown, quickReplies, picker, image, card, form, and more
-   `customData` - Opaque blob that must be preserved and returned unchanged

#### Output format (chat agent to Contact Center)

Your chat agent must return responses in this format.

```json
{
    "id": "resp-001",
    "sessionId": "sess-abc-123",
    "body": [{ "type": "text", "value": "Hi, I'm your virtual agent!" }],
    "timestamp": 1700000001000,
    "userId": "user-xyz-789",
    "completed": false,
    "customData": { "...": "write back as-is" }
}
```

Required fields:

-   `userId` - Must match the request value exactly
-   `customData` - Must match the request value exactly (treat as opaque, never parse or modify)
-   `completed` - Set to `false` to continue conversation, `true` to end and proceed to next flow step

> **Don't parse customData**
>
> Always pass `customData` through unchanged. It contains anti-forgery tokens and internal state that may change across versions. Never parse, validate, or construct customData fields.

### Script examples

The following examples show common transformation script patterns for different integration scenarios.

#### Pass-through for trigger support

Use this script when your chat agent supports asynchronous responses via triggers.

```javascript
zm.log.info("Action script start - pass-through");

const {
    id,
    sessionId,
    conversationMode,
    message,
    conversationVariables,
    additionalPayload,
    languageCode,
    timestamp,
    userId,
    customData,
} = ctx.inputData;

const myCustomData = customData; // Save to pass back unchanged in response

const result = await zm.fetch({
    url: "/send_message_to_bot",
    method: "POST",
    data: {
        id,
        sessionId,
        conversationMode,
        message,
        conversationVariables,
        additionalPayload,
        languageCode,
        timestamp,
        userId,
        customData,
    },
});

return zm.handleResponse(
    result,
    (body) => {
        zm.log.info("Virtual agent response received");
        body.customData = myCustomData;
        return body;
    },
    (code, msg, body) => {
        zm.log.error("Request failed. Code: {}, message: {}", code, msg);
        return zm.errorResponse(code, msg, body);
    },
);
```

#### Custom format transformation

Use this script when your chat agent uses a different API format and returns responses synchronously.

If your chat agent expects this format:

```json
{
    "botMessage": { "type": "text", "value": "hi" },
    "session": "sess-abc-123",
    "user": "user-xyz-789",
    "time": 1700000000000,
    "mode": "START_CONVERSATION",
    "lang": "en-US",
    "variables": {},
    "payload": null
}
```

And returns this format:

```json
{
    "messageId": "bot-resp-001",
    "replyText": "Response text",
    "isComplete": false
}
```

Use this transformation script:

```javascript
zm.log.info("Action script start - custom transformation");

const {
    id,
    sessionId,
    conversationMode,
    message,
    conversationVariables,
    additionalPayload,
    languageCode,
    timestamp,
    userId,
    customData,
} = ctx.inputData;

const myCustomData = customData; // Save to pass back unchanged in response

const result = await zm.fetch({
    url: "/send_message_to_bot",
    method: "POST",
    data: {
        botMessage: message,
        session: sessionId,
        user: userId,
        time: timestamp,
        mode: conversationMode,
        lang: languageCode,
        variables: conversationVariables,
        payload: additionalPayload,
    },
});

return zm.handleResponse(
    result,
    (body) => {
        zm.log.info(
            "Virtual agent response received, transforming to Contact Center format",
        );
        return {
            id: body.messageId || id,
            sessionId: sessionId,
            body: [{ type: "text", value: body.replyText }],
            timestamp: Date.now(),
            userId: userId,
            completed: body.isComplete || false,
            customData: myCustomData,
        };
    },
    (code, msg, body) => {
        zm.log.error("Request failed. Code: {}, message: {}", code, msg);
        return zm.errorResponse(code, msg, body);
    },
);
```

## Configure the trigger (for asynchronous responses)

Triggers allow your chat agent to push responses back to Contact Center asynchronously when processing takes longer than the action timeout allows. Triggers must always be paired with an action. The action initiates the request to your chat agent, and the trigger provides an asynchronous response channel for your chat agent to send replies back when processing is complete.

### Create a static webhook

Create an incoming webhook that your chat agent will call to send asynchronous responses.

1. In the navigation pane, choose **Connect**.
2. Choose **Incoming webhooks**.
3. Choose **+ New incoming webhook**.
4. Configure your webhook settings.
5. Choose **Save changes**.

When using triggers, your chat agent must include the `customData` object from the original action request in the webhook callback. Contact Center uses this data to route the response to the correct conversation.

> **Note**
>
> One app can have at most one `zcc.chatbot_send_message_to_bot` action and one `zcc.bot_message` trigger.

## Test the integration

Test your integration in two stages: first validate the app configuration in Zoom Marketplace, then test the complete conversation flow in the Contact Center admin portal.

### Test in Zoom Marketplace

Validate your endpoint configuration and transformation script in Zoom Marketplace where you created your app.

1. In the navigation pane, choose **Connect**.
2. Choose **Base URL & authentication**.
3. In the **Test connection** section, choose **+ Add connection** to create a test connection.
4. Use the test connection to validate endpoint connectivity.
5. In the navigation pane, choose **Actions and Triggers**.
6. Open your action and use the **Test** step with sample input to verify your transformation logic.

### Create a production connection

Create a production connection in Zoom Marketplace that you'll use in your Contact Center flow.

1. In the navigation pane, choose **Connect**.
2. Choose **Base URL & authentication**.
3. Choose **+ Add connection** to create a new connection with your chat agent's production credentials.

### Test in the admin portal

Test the complete conversation flow from consumer interaction through chat agent response and agent handoff in the Contact Center admin portal.

1. Sign in to the [Zoom admin portal](https://admin.zoom.us/).
2. In the navigation pane, choose **Contact Center Management**.
3. Choose **Flows**.
4. Create a flow with a Bot node that uses your production connection.
5. Configure a Queue and Entry Point for the flow.
6. Initiate a test conversation as a consumer.
7. Verify chat agent responses and conversation flow.
8. If your chat agent supports handoff, test the transition to a live agent.

After successful testing, publish your app on Zoom Marketplace to make it available for installation by Contact Center admins.
